complexity_rationale: Sole writer of orders.status (ADR-003) AND owner of the §9.2 state machine across 8 states + 14 allowed transitions + 14 explicitly forbidden ones AND consumer of 4 cross-topic events (events.payment.completed/failed/expired + events.reservation.expired) AND producer of events.order.cancelled via outbox AND recipient of two formally-authored internal endpoints (order.create-from-checkout, order.cancel-on-checkout-failure) per ADR-007's checkout compensation matrix. State-driven consumer rule (ADR-009: read current row state via SELECT FOR UPDATE; ignore event.fromStatus) is load-bearing for the PR-003 cross-topic race; mis-implementing it permanently corrupts orders.

summary.responsibility: Sole writer of order lifecycle state. Owns orders + order_items (immutable price/name/image snapshots per ORD-007), per-transition order_status_history (ORD-009), human-readable order numbers (ORD-008), the outbox emission for events.order.cancelled, and the four state-driven inbound event consumers. Consumes payment + inventory events to drive the §9.2 state machine.
summary.sole_writer_invariant: Per ADR-003 + contracts.json notes.locked_decisions_summary line 12 + PR-003 race resolution: Order is the ONLY service that writes orders.status. Payment, Inventory, and Checkout never UPDATE orders.status directly. Checkout creates the row in PENDING_PAYMENT via the internal endpoint order.create-from-checkout; thereafter every status mutation passes through Order's state-machine guard (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE -> validate transition table -> write status_history -> maybe emit outbox).

tables.name: orders
tables.purpose: Aggregate root. One row per customer order. Sole-writer of orders.status (ADR-003).

columns.name: id
columns.notes: UUID v7 client-supplied by Checkout (per cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule). Recipient stores as-is; does NOT call uuid_generate_v7() on this column. Sortable by creation time.

columns.name: order_number
columns.notes: Human-readable per ORD-008. Format: ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN. See order_number_strategy below. Allocated server-side at create-from-checkout time.

columns.name: user_id
columns.notes: Owner; supplied as customerUserId by Checkout (claims.sub from Checkout's inbound JWT). Used by order.list-mine and ownership check on order.detail / order.cancel-mine.

columns.name: status
columns.notes: ADR-003 sole-writer field. Modified ONLY by service/order_lifecycle inside SELECT ... FOR UPDATE tx. Code comment at every UPDATE: '// ADR-003 sole-writer of orders.status'.

columns.name: subtotal
columns.notes: Whole-THB integer (cross-cutting.pricing currency rule). Snapshot at commit; immutable thereafter.

columns.name: shipping_fee
columns.notes: Snapshot at commit. Per cross-cutting.pricing tier rule (1500 THB inclusive boundary -> free; otherwise 60 THB).

columns.name: coupon_discount
columns.notes: Coupon engine out_of_scope; reserved field, must be 0 in this run (defensive CHECK).

columns.name: grand_total
columns.notes: = subtotal + shipping_fee - coupon_discount per cross-cutting.pricing.formula. Snapshot; equals payment intent amount.

columns.name: currency
columns.notes: MVP THB-only; CHECK is defensive.

columns.name: address_snapshot
columns.notes: Frozen Address payload at commit-time {addressId, receiverName, phone, addressLine, province, district, postalCode}. Used by order.detail; never re-resolved from identity.address.list. ORD-007 immutability.

columns.name: buyer_email_snapshot
columns.notes: Per contract order.list-admin.notes (contracts.json line 985) and Plan-Reviewer PR-002 advisory: SNAPSHOT IS PER-ORDER, NOT PER-LINE-ITEM. Captured at create-from-checkout time from the buyerEmail request field (Checkout sourced via identity.profile.read in checkout.commit step 2 — REV-L2-001 fix). Backs admin search-by-email.

columns.name: tracking_number
columns.notes: Set on PACKING->SHIPPED transition; required for that transition (ORD-006). NULL until SHIPPED.

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.notes: Replay correlation. Equals Idempotency-Key header == orderId per cross-cutting.idempotency.internal_orderId_rule. Stored for trace/debug; the de-facto idempotency key is orders.id itself (so duplicate INSERT raises a PK violation that the handler treats as a replay).

columns.name: version
columns.notes: Optimistic-lock column (OPTLOCK). Bumped on every UPDATE. Belt-and-suspenders alongside SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; the FOR UPDATE is the binding mechanism (cross-cutting.persistence.concurrency).

columns.name: updated_at
columns.notes: Bumped on every UPDATE in the repo write path.

indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_id_created_at_desc ON orders (user_id, created_at DESC) -- backs order.list-mine sort+filter.
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status_created_at_desc ON orders (status, created_at DESC) -- backs order.list-admin status filter.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_orders_order_number ON orders (order_number).
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_buyer_email_lower ON orders (LOWER(buyer_email_snapshot)) -- case-insensitive admin search-by-email.

tables.name: order_items
tables.purpose: Line items. Snapshot fields are IMMUTABLE per ORD-007.

columns.name: name_snapshot
columns.notes: Frozen at commit; product later soft-deleted still resolves here (CAT-009).

columns.name: image_url_snapshot
columns.notes: Frozen at commit. NULL acceptable — products may have no image.

columns.name: price_snapshot
columns.notes: Whole-THB integer; the price at commit-time. ORD-007 immutability invariant — repo exposes no Update method.

columns.name: line_subtotal
columns.notes: = price_snapshot * qty; persisted (denormalized) for audit/replay independence from arithmetic drift.

indexes: INDEX idx_order_items_order_id ON order_items (order_id) -- backs order.detail JOIN.
tables.immutability_enforcement: Repo layer exposes NO Update method (ORD-007). Defensive Postgres trigger on UPDATE/DELETE raises 'order_items rows are immutable per ORD-007' (deferred — repo discipline + code review covers MVP).

tables.name: order_status_history
tables.purpose: Append-only audit row per transition (ORD-009). Written in the SAME tx as the orders.status UPDATE (or, for the initial PENDING_PAYMENT row, the orders INSERT).

columns.name: from_status
columns.notes: NULL only for the initial PENDING_PAYMENT row written by order.create-from-checkout.

columns.name: actor_user_id
columns.notes: NULL when actor_role='SYSTEM' (event-driven transitions or checkout-compensation).

columns.name: reason
columns.notes: Required by app logic when to_status='CANCELLED' (admin path) or for SYSTEM transitions where the origin event id is recorded ('reservation expired (TTL) eventId=...' / 'payment.failed eventId=...' / 'payment intent creation failed: <upstream code>').

indexes: INDEX idx_order_status_history_order_occurred ON order_status_history (order_id, occurred_at ASC) -- backs order.detail.statusHistory ordering.

tables.name: outbox_events
tables.purpose: Per ADR-004 outbox pattern + cross-cutting.persistence.outbox_pattern. Written in the SAME tx as the status mutation when emitting events.order.cancelled OR (per contracts.json line 1067) the audit-only PENDING_PAYMENT event on creation.

columns.name: id
columns.notes: UUID v7; doubles as event_id in the published payload.

columns.name: aggregate_id
columns.notes: = orders.id. Becomes the Kafka partition key (events.order.cancelled.ordering_guarantees: partition_key = orderId).

columns.name: event_type
columns.notes: MVP: 'order.cancelled' (consumed by inventory + payment) and 'order.created' (audit-only PENDING_PAYMENT signal — no consumer in MVP).

columns.name: payload_json
columns.notes: Conforms to events.order.cancelled.payload {eventId, occurredAt, orderId, cancelActor, fromStatus, reason?} for cancel events; audit-only payload for the create event.

columns.name: published_at
columns.notes: NULL until the publisher goroutine sends to Kafka.

indexes: CREATE INDEX outbox_events_pending ON outbox_events (id) WHERE published_at IS NULL -- partial index for the publisher polling query (ADR-004).

tables.name: consumed_events
tables.purpose: Per-service idempotency table for inbound Kafka events (events.payment.completed | events.payment.failed | events.payment.expired | events.reservation.expired). PK on event_id; INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING absorbs at-least-once redelivery (ADR-004).

columns.name: event_id
columns.notes: Conflict on insert = duplicate; consumer treats as already-processed and acks.

columns.name: consumer_name
columns.notes: e.g. 'order.payment.completed' / 'order.payment.failed' / 'order.payment.expired' / 'order.reservation.expired'.

columns.name: order_id
columns.notes: For debug; the actual transition uses the order_id from the event payload.

tables.name: admin_action_log
tables.purpose: Local audit log for admin endpoints per Reviewer-L1 quality bar. Audit-as-its-own-service is out_of_scope (BA out_of_scope line 76); admin endpoints still log to a local table; the row is written in-tx with the status mutation.

columns.name: endpoint
columns.notes: e.g. 'order.update-status-admin' / 'order.list-admin'.

columns.name: order_id
columns.notes: NULL for endpoints that don't act on a specific order (list-admin).

columns.name: request_summary
columns.notes: {toStatus?, trackingNumber?, reason?, filters?} -- never includes the JWT or auth header (security review item).

columns.name: outcome_code
columns.notes: From cross-cutting.error-codes registry (e.g. SUCCESS, INVALID_ORDER_STATE).

indexes: INDEX idx_admin_action_log_order_occurred ON admin_action_log (order_id, occurred_at DESC) WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL -- forensics.

order_number_strategy.chosen_implementation: Single global Postgres sequence formatted into a date prefix at allocation time.
order_number_strategy.ddl: CREATE SEQUENCE order_number_seq START 1 INCREMENT 1 NO CYCLE;
order_number_strategy.rationale: A per-day sequence requires either DDL at midnight or a sequence-per-day naming scheme (operationally noisy in MVP). A single global sequence formatted with NNNNNN zero-padded to 6 digits (overflow tolerated as 7+ once we cross 10^6 orders) keeps allocation a single, race-free SELECT nextval(...) and meets ORD-008's only stated requirement (human-readable, includes a date). Trade-off: NNNNNN does not reset to 000001 at midnight, but ORD-008 does not require that — only the ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN shape.
order_number_strategy.allocation: Inside order.create-from-checkout tx: SELECT nextval('order_number_seq'); format as fmt.Sprintf('ORD-%s-%06d', time.Now().UTC().Format('20060102'), seq). Race-free by sequence semantics; UNIQUE constraint on order_number is the safety net.
alternatives_considered_and_rejected: (b) per-day sequence: needs a daily DDL job or table-driven counter under FOR UPDATE -- extra complexity for no MVP benefit.
(c) UUID v7 as order_number: not human-readable; violates ORD-008 spirit.
(d) snowflake-style ID inside Order: adds a clock-skew failure mode; sequence is the simplest safe pick.

error_contract.trigger: id not found OR not owned by claims.sub
current status != PENDING_PAYMENT (ORD-004; e.g. attempting to cancel a PAID order via this endpoint)

edge_behavior.idempotency: Re-cancelling a CANCELLED-by-self order returns 200 (per contract idempotency_rules + AMBIG-ORD-3 resolution). The handler checks the latest status_history row's actor_user_id == claims.sub; if so, 200 idempotent. If the latest cancel was by ADMIN, the customer gets 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE because they no longer own the action.
side_effects: UPDATE orders SET status='CANCELLED', version+=1, updated_at=now()  // ADR-003 sole-writer of orders.status
INSERT outbox_events (event_type='order.cancelled', payload {eventId, occurredAt, orderId, cancelActor:'CUSTOMER', fromStatus:'PENDING_PAYMENT'})
edge_behavior.transactionality: Single tx; SELECT FOR UPDATE on the orders row before validating + writing.

endpoints.transition_guarded: PENDING_PAYMENT -> CANCELLED only (ORD-004). Any other current status returns INVALID_ORDER_STATE.
transaction_steps: 1. BEGIN;
2. SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id=$1 AND user_id=claims.sub FOR UPDATE; — combined ownership + lock. NOT FOUND -> ROLLBACK; 404 ORDER_NOT_OWNED (do NOT 403; preserves enumeration resistance).

3. If status='CANCELLED': read most-recent status_history row; if its actor_user_id = claims.sub -> COMMIT; return 200 (idempotent re-cancel by self per AMBIG-ORD-3 resolution). Else ROLLBACK; 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE.
4. If status != 'PENDING_PAYMENT' -> ROLLBACK; 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE.
5. UPDATE orders SET status='CANCELLED', version=version+1, updated_at=now() WHERE id=$1 AND version=$old_version; -- ADR-003 sole-writer.
6. INSERT INTO order_status_history (order_id, from_status='PENDING_PAYMENT', to_status='CANCELLED', actor_user_id=claims.sub, actor_role='CUSTOMER', reason=NULL);

7. INSERT INTO outbox_events (id=uuidv7(), aggregate_id=order_id, event_type='order.cancelled', payload_json={eventId:id, occurredAt:now(), orderId:order_id, cancelActor:'CUSTOMER', fromStatus:'PENDING_PAYMENT', reason:null});
8. COMMIT;
endpoints.side_effects_summary: status_history row + outbox order.cancelled with fromStatus=PENDING_PAYMENT. Inventory consumes and releases reservation (RESERVED->available). Payment intent transitions to CANCELLED via its own state-driven consumer.

Optional Idempotency-Key per contract; if supplied, the standard idempotency_keys store applies (out-of-band; not implemented in MVP since the FOR UPDATE + status-comparison achieves the same property).

endpoints.transition_table_reference: state_machine.allowed_transitions filtered to ADMIN-actor rows (5 rows). The handler validates the (currentStatus, toStatus) pair against this table AFTER acquiring the row lock, NEVER from a stale read.
transaction_steps: 1. Validate role=ADMIN (transport/http admin decorator); reject CUSTOMER with 403 AUTH_FORBIDDEN.
2. Validate request shape: trackingNumber when toStatus=SHIPPED; reason when toStatus=CANCELLED. Else 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.
3. BEGIN;
4. SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE; NOT FOUND -> ROLLBACK; 404 NOT_FOUND.

5. If status = toStatus already (idempotent retry per contract idempotency_rules) -> INSERT admin_action_log {outcome_code='SUCCESS', request_summary:{idempotent:true}}; COMMIT no-op (no extra status_history row, no extra outbox row); return 200.

6. Look up (current_status, toStatus, ADMIN) in state_machine.allowed_transitions. Miss -> INSERT admin_action_log {outcome_code='INVALID_ORDER_STATE', ...}; COMMIT (audit even on rejection); return 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE.

7. Apply side_effects per the transition row: UPDATE orders SET status=$2, tracking_number=$3 if SHIPPED, version=version+1; INSERT order_status_history; if toStatus=CANCELLED INSERT outbox_events (event_type='order.cancelled', payload {fromStatus:current_status, cancelActor:'ADMIN', reason}).
8. INSERT admin_action_log {outcome_code='SUCCESS', ...}.
9. COMMIT.
endpoints.notes: PAID is reachable only via events.payment.completed consumer; PENDING_PAYMENT only via order.create-from-checkout; PAYMENT_FAILED/PAYMENT_EXPIRED only via the corresponding event consumers. This admin endpoint cannot synthesize those states — see explicitly_disallowed examples in state_machine.

1. Validate Idempotency-Key == request.orderId; mismatch -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (REV-L2-006).
2. Validate body against schema; recompute subtotal + total; mismatch -> 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.
3. BEGIN;
4. Try INSERT INTO orders (id=$orderId, ...) ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id;

5. If no row returned (duplicate orderId): SELECT existing row + order_items; compute request_hash and compare to stored idempotency_key + body. If equal body -> COMMIT; return original 200 envelope. If different body -> ROLLBACK; 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED with originalOrderNumber.
6. Else (fresh INSERT succeeded): SELECT nextval('order_number_seq') -> format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN. UPDATE orders SET order_number=$1 WHERE id=$2.
7. INSERT INTO order_items (one row per request.items[i]; price_snapshot/name_snapshot/image_url_snapshot frozen here).
8. INSERT INTO order_status_history (from_status=NULL, to_status='PENDING_PAYMENT', actor_role='SYSTEM', actor_user_id=NULL, reason='checkout.commit step 7').
9. INSERT INTO outbox_events (event_type='order.created', aggregate_id=$orderId, payload_json={audit-only PENDING_PAYMENT signal}). [Per contracts.json line 1067 — no consumer in MVP.]
10. COMMIT;

Order MUST reject CUSTOMER and ADMIN tokens on this endpoint (a customer fabricating an order body would bypass server-priced checkout). pseudocode: INSERT INTO consumed_events(event_id=evt.eventId, consumer_name='order.payment.completed', event_type='payment.completed', order_id=evt.orderId)
ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING event_id
if no row returned: COMMIT; ack; return  // dedup hit, already processed
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id=evt.orderId FOR UPDATE
if not found: COMMIT; log_warn('payment.completed for unknown orderId'); ack; return  // defensive — order schema is sole owner
log_info('late payment.completed for non-PENDING_PAYMENT order, status=' + status)
COMMIT; ack; return  // state-driven no-op per events.payment.completed.failure_modes Order branch
UPDATE orders SET status='PAID', version=version+1, updated_at=now() WHERE id=evt.orderId  // ADR-003 sole-writer
INSERT INTO order_status_history (order_id, from_status='PENDING_PAYMENT', to_status='PAID', actor_role='SYSTEM', actor_user_id=NULL, reason='payment.completed eventId=' + evt.eventId)

deduplication_with_reservation_expired.scenario: Both events.payment.expired (Payment) and events.reservation.expired (Inventory sweeper) can drive PENDING_PAYMENT -> PAYMENT_EXPIRED for the same order. They are produced by different services on different Kafka topics, so cross-topic ordering is NOT preserved (ADR-009).
deduplication_with_reservation_expired.resolution: First-writer-wins, enforced atomically by SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the orders row inside each consumer's tx. The first event to acquire the row lock observes status='PENDING_PAYMENT' and performs the transition; the second event observes status='PAYMENT_EXPIRED' and falls into the state-driven no-op branch (logs and acks).
deduplication_with_reservation_expired.history_row_distinguishes_origin: The reason field of the order_status_history row preserves which event won the race ('payment.expired eventId=...' vs 'reservation expired (TTL) eventId=... reservationId=...'). Operators reading order.detail.statusHistory can see exactly which path expired the order.
deduplication_with_reservation_expired.no_double_emission: Order emits no outbox event for PAYMENT_EXPIRED transitions, so there is no risk of double-publishing downstream. Inventory's reservation release is the single stock-side effect (already issued by the sweeper or by Payment's earlier consumer fan-out).
deduplication_with_reservation_expired.test_required: QA must include a PR-008 e2e test: customer hits checkout.commit, never simulates payment. After RESERVATION_TTL_MINUTES + sweep cadence, exactly one of {payment.expired, reservation.expired} writes the PAYMENT_EXPIRED status_history row and the other is recorded as a logged no-op in service logs.

event_producers.emit_path: outbox_events row written in same tx as orders UPDATE; transport/outbox_publisher goroutine ships to Kafka
emitted_when: order.update-status-admin (toStatus=CANCELLED) succeeds for either fromStatus=PENDING_PAYMENT or fromStatus=PAID; cancelActor=ADMIN; reason=$request.reason
event_producers.outbox_pattern: Per ADR-004 + cross-cutting.persistence.outbox_pattern. The outbox_events row is INSERTED in the SAME tx as the orders UPDATE and the order_status_history INSERT — so the trio commits atomically. A separate publisher goroutine polls outbox_events WHERE published_at IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 100, ships via common/kafka, then sets published_at.
event_producers.payload_conformance: Strictly matches events.order.cancelled.payload_shape: {eventId (UUID v7), occurredAt (RFC3339), orderId, cancelActor (CUSTOMER|ADMIN|SYSTEM), fromStatus (PENDING_PAYMENT|PAID), reason?}.

state_machine.concurrency_invariant: EVERY transition (customer, admin, or event-driven) is implemented as: BEGIN tx -> SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE -> look up (current_status, target_status, actor) in allowed_transitions -> if miss return INVALID_ORDER_STATE (or no-op for state-driven consumers) -> UPDATE orders + INSERT order_status_history + (maybe) INSERT outbox_events -> COMMIT. The optimistic version column is bumped as a defensive belt-and-suspenders alongside the FOR UPDATE row lock (cross-cutting.persistence.concurrency).

actor_authority_matrix.CUSTOMER: May only drive PENDING_PAYMENT -> CANCELLED on owned orders.
actor_authority_matrix.ADMIN: May drive PAID->PACKING, PACKING->SHIPPED (trackingNumber required), SHIPPED->DELIVERED, PENDING_PAYMENT->CANCELLED (reason required), PAID->CANCELLED (reason required).
actor_authority_matrix.SYSTEM: May drive PENDING_PAYMENT -> {PAID, PAYMENT_FAILED, PAYMENT_EXPIRED, CANCELLED-by-checkout-compensation}; never drives admin transitions.

test_strategy.unit: Table-driven tests with pgxmock or testcontainers Postgres. domain/transitions exhaustively covered: 8 statuses x 8 statuses x 3 actors (192 cells) — assert each cell maps to allowed_transitions or returns ErrInvalidOrderState; no other transition silently allowed. service/order_number_allocator: format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN; zero-padding; date prefix matches now().UTC(). Consumer state-machine guards: for each of the 4 inbound event types, simulate the 8 possible current_status values and assert the transition or no-op outcome.
test_strategy.integration: Per-endpoint repo+http integration tests on a Postgres testcontainer + an embedded Kafka via testcontainers. order.create-from-checkout: assert orders + 1+ order_items + initial status_history row + audit outbox row commit atomically; rollback on any insert error leaves no partial state. Idempotent replay with same body returns original orderNumber; replay with different body returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED with original orderNumber in error data. order.cancel-mine: assert orders.status='CANCELLED', status_history row, outbox_events row commit atomically; outbox_events.published_at NULL until publisher polls. order.update-status-admin: walk PAID->PACKING->SHIPPED(trackingNumber)->DELIVERED; assert each writes a status_history row + admin_action_log row; assert SHIPPED without trackingNumber returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR; assert DELIVERED->CANCELLED returns 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE.
load_or_chaos: Outbox publisher backpressure: pause Kafka, generate 1000 cancelled events, resume Kafka — assert all 1000 are eventually published exactly once (Inventory's consumer dedup is the safety net for any redelivery).

Concurrency: spawn N goroutines that all attempt order.cancel-mine on the same PENDING_PAYMENT order; assert exactly one succeeds, the rest receive 200 idempotent or 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE; assert exactly one outbox row written.

chosen_order_creation_path.selected: (a) order.create-from-checkout — Order exposes a private endpoint that only Checkout calls, gated by transport/internal_auth (X-Internal-Secret + INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET; ADR-008).
chosen_order_creation_path.rationale: The contracts pin (a): contracts.json line 269 (cross-cutting.persistence.transactional_boundaries.checkout.commit) and line 913 (checkout.commit.internal_orchestration step 7) both name 'order.create-from-checkout' as a SYNC HTTP call from Checkout. Path (b) (event-driven create) defeats UX — frontend must navigate to the payment-mock screen with the orderId in hand. Path (c) (Checkout INSERTs directly) violates ADR-003 (Order is sole writer). Path (a) keeps the synchronous response while preserving the sole-writer invariant — Order owns the INSERT and the initial PENDING_PAYMENT history row.
chosen_order_creation_path.compensation_path: Path (a) also requires the matching internal endpoint order.cancel-on-checkout-failure (contracts.json line 920; ADR-007 explicit requirement) so Checkout can roll the order to CANCELLED if a downstream sync call (e.g. payment.intent.create) fails AFTER the order row was created. Both internal endpoints are first-class endpoints[] entries in this td.json — neither is a stub (REV-L2-004 closure).

internal_auth_pattern.env_var_name: INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET (the only accepted name; ADR-008; recipient refuses to boot if read from any other env-var name)
internal_auth_pattern.comparison: crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(supplied), []byte(secret)) == 1 (ADR-008; plain == / != is FORBIDDEN — Reviewer-L1/L2 grep blocks it)
internal_auth_pattern.min_length: 32 bytes (256 bits of entropy); recipient validates length at startup; refuses to boot if shorter
internal_auth_pattern.rotation_overlap: INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET MAY accept comma-separated 'new,old'; recipient tries ConstantTimeCompare against each segment; first match wins
internal_auth_pattern.audit_logging: On reject: slog.Error('internal_auth_reject', remoteAddr, x_forwarded_for, path, requestId) — NEVER log the supplied/expected value. On startup: slog.Info('internal_auth_configured', service='order', sha256_prefix=hex(sha256(secret))[:8]).
internal_auth_pattern.frontend_posture: frontend MUST NOT load INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET nor forward X-Internal-Secret (REV-L2-013; cross-checked by frontend regression test)

contract_ambiguity_flags.observation: order.cancel-mine.idempotency_rules says 're-cancelling a CANCELLED-by-self order returns 200'. Implication: re-cancelling a CANCELLED-by-admin order via order.cancel-mine should NOT silently 200; it should return INVALID_ORDER_STATE because CANCELLED is terminal and the customer no longer owns the action. This td.json implements: idempotent 200 only when the most-recent status_history row's actor_user_id matches claims.sub, else 409. Reviewer-L1 to confirm.
